messages:
marie: heads up — found a routing gap when a project-scoped API key is proxied via the edge proxy. quota attribution falls back to org instead of project. noticed in canary traffic this morning

devon: ugh, seen it. is this the case where token-exchange loses the original project_claim?

alex: yes — the exchange flow rewrites the token and we only persist the service_account id. project_claim was marked as ephemeral and not forwarded in the header.

lisa: quick question: is this causing billing mismatches or just telemetry gaps?

marie: both. billing shows org-level usage spikes for a handful of customers. telemetry traces show missing project tags for ~2.3% of calls in canary.

devon: repro steps? I can try a small test.

marie: repro is: 1) use project-scoped API key
2) go through edge-proxy with exchange enabled
3) call /v1/generate. you should see header X-Orig-Project missing after proxy

alex: here is the relevant snippet from the exchange lambda:

```
// we replace token with service principal
const out = await exchangeToken(incoming);
context.set('x-project', out.project || null);
return proxyPass(out.token);
```

we assumed out.project only present for direct keys, not for delegated flows.

lisa: sounds like we need two fixes: (A) ensure exchange preserves origin metadata, (B) add a fallback reconciliation job that tags historical requests by matching session ids. which do we prioritize?

devon: A first. small change in exchange to copy origin_claims if present. low risk. then add a feature flag to roll it out.

alex: agree. canary the flag on a subset of edge nodes. also add a unit test: assert that introspect(incoming).origin.project === header.x-orig-project after exchange.

marie: also want console UX: customers are confused when their project dashboard shows no usage while org shows it. can we add a temporary telemetry note? maybe show a banner "Possible attribution gap" with a link to support.

lisa: ok. ops question: how will quotas behave during the fix? if attribution changes mid-rollout, quotas might start applying at project-level instead of org-level, and customers could hit lower limits unexpectedly.

devon: good call. plan: when we flip the flag, keep quota enforcement on the old key of record for 48h, but surface the new project attribution in read-only telemetry. after 48h we switch enforcement to project. that gives owners time to adjust quota configs.

marie: does the console need a migration button? some large customers might want to opt-out of retroactive enforcement.

alex: yeah add an org-level toggle in the billing/quotas page: "Use project-attribution for delegated tokens (rollout)" defaulting to off during the 48h window.

sre-bot: incident risk: low -> medium. suggested alert: delta in project vs org usage > 5% across 10m.

marie: telemetry work: add sampling tags for all exchange requests (add header X-Exchange-Trace) and ensure traces include original project id when available. also emit metric `auth.exchange.missing_project_count`.

devon: I'll open a PR for the exchange change and add the feature flag. alex can handle tests + proxy rollout. lisa can wire the console banner + toggle. marie will add telemetry/alert runbook.

lisa: timeline?

devon: PR by EOD today, internal canary tomorrow AM, dashboard banner staged by noon. full rollout gated on metric drop to <0.5% missing_project for 24h.

marie: noted. tagging @support for customer comms draft.

auth-bot: new ticket created: AUTH-1327 "Preserve project_claim in token exchange + canary rollout plan" assigned to devon.

marie: thanks — will follow up in morning stand. :thumbsup:

alex: small follow-up: if we preserve project_claim in headers, ensure we strip it before logging request bodies in case of PII. add rule in zap middleware.

devon: good catch. will add middleware scrubber.

lisa: added a short note to the console banner copy: "We are rolling out improved project-level attribution; during the rollout you may see temporary quota behavior. See details -> [link]"

marie: ok closing thread; will post final rollout status later. :eyes:
